name: tooltip
purpose: Surfaces a short hint anchored to a trigger element when the user hovers, focuses, or long-presses it. Use for icon-only buttons, abbreviations, or any control whose meaning is not obvious from its label alone. **Not** for rich content or interactive children — use `popover` instead.
useWhen: Use Tooltip for a one-line plain-text name or hint on a control, shown on hover or focus; it cannot hold links. For rich or interactive content opened by a click use Popover; for a read-only rich preview on hover use HoverCard.
Naming an icon-only control on hover and focus.
Revealing the full text of a truncated label, or expanding an abbreviation.
One short, plain-text hint that the user can do without.
avoidWhen: The content has links, buttons or more than one line of structure → use `popover`.
An info glyph beside a field label or column header → use `hint`.
A read-only rich preview (a definition, a glossed term in documentation prose) → use `hover-card`.
Guidance or errors the user needs to complete a field → use `field-error`.
related: popover` — click-opened, interactive, with a header, body and footer.
hint` — the focusable info glyph that renders a `Tooltip` for you.
hover-card` — read-only rich preview on hover or focus; DocMarkdown's `<Tooltip>` tag renders one.
icon-button` — the most common trigger; it still needs its own `ariaLabel`.
bestPractices: Wrap a focusable element. The tooltip opens on the wrapper's `focusin`, and the wrapper itself is not focusable.
Keep `content` to a few words. It renders as plain text, with no markup.
The tooltip describes its trigger (`aria-describedby`) but does not name it. Icon-only triggers still need their own accessible name.
Use `disabled` to suppress the tooltip. An empty `content` also blocks opening, but it reads as a bug.
Keep the default `delay` (200 ms) unless a dense toolbar needs a longer one.

Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.

props.name: content
props.doc: Plain text shown inside the tooltip.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Anchor side relative to the trigger; `auto` picks the side with room.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The trigger element. Tooltip anchors to its bounding box.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Button from '@aziontech/webkit/button'
  import Tooltip from '@aziontech/webkit/tooltip'
</script>

<template>
  <Tooltip
    content="This is a Tooltip"
    placement="top"
  >
    <Button
      label="Hover me"
      variant="outline"
      size="medium"
    />
  </Tooltip>
</template>
